proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.priority: P0—resolved source-role confusion; rationale/context precision review remains
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.disposition: KEEP THE EXISTING AT-LEAST-25% ANSWER. Do not apply the formerly suggested >25% scoring threshold here: the stem asks about obstructive hypoventilation, and the 2023 ICSD-3-TR correction sheet gives at least 25% for the pediatric OSA obstructive hypoventilation diagnostic pattern. Proposed improvement is source-specific stem/rationale only; stage remains held pending clinical/editorial review.
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.proposedAnswer: CO2 greater than 50 mm Hg for at least 25% of total sleep time with obstructive features
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.proposedRationale: The ICSD-3-TR pediatric OSA diagnostic criteria describe an obstructive hypoventilation pattern with hypercapnia (PaCO2 greater than 50 mm Hg) during at least 25% of total sleep time, together with features such as snoring, inspiratory flow flattening or paradoxical thoracoabdominal movement. Do not substitute the separate AASM pediatric hypoventilation event-scoring duration threshold for this diagnostic pattern. PSG scoring uses the applicable current AASM manual; diagnosis rests with the interpreting clinician.
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.why: Directly checked user-supplied 2023 ICSD-3-TR supplemental correction PDF page 3: its revised pediatric OSA diagnostic Criterion B(2) explicitly says AT LEAST 25%. FST3 Chapter 61 split PDF volume 4 p40 prints an older (v2.5) PSG pediatric hypoventilation SCORING rule with MORE THAN 25%. The prior review incorrectly treated the two source types as interchangeable. The existing answer matches the ICSD-3-TR obstructive diagnostic context, so do not change its option or answer.

proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.proposedRationale: A pediatric hypopnea requires the applicable airflow-reduction duration and measurement criteria as well as an associated qualifying desaturation or arousal. The question isolates the associated 3% SpO2 threshold; meeting that threshold alone is not sufficient to score the event. Confirm the complete definition against the licensed AASM Version 3 pediatric scoring rules.
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.why: Correct answer tests desaturation threshold, but stem uses 'is scored ... if' and rationale omits the pediatric event-duration rule; risk of overgeneralization.

existing.prompt: According to AASM pediatric scoring rules, a respiratory event is scored as a hypopnea if the amplitude drops by at least 30% and is associated with an arousal, an awakening, or a drop in SpO2 of at least:
existing.rationale: Pediatric hypopnea criteria use a >=30% amplitude reduction plus an arousal, awakening, or >=3% desaturation.

proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.disposition: propose clarified case wording after current licensed scoring-manual review, while retaining the answer
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.proposedPrompt: A child has absent airflow and absent respiratory effort for at least two missed breaths but less than 20 seconds, with a qualifying associated arousal. Which interpretation best fits the appropriate pediatric scoring pathway?
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.proposedAnswer: It may still meet pediatric central apnea criteria
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.proposedRationale: Unlike a blanket adult 10-second approach, pediatric central apnea criteria may capture events shorter than 20 seconds when the required two-breath duration and associated qualifying consequence are documented. Verify the exact current threshold and event conditions against AASM Version 3 before publication.
proposedRuleSensitiveRevisions.why: Existing case only says less than 20 seconds, without confirming the two-missed-breath minimum. Other current learner questions test the same decision family (src32-026, case-d3-010).
